flags: Spelling of the 'distinct' value: SPEC R-017 says 'distinct'; r2#22 and the v2.6 code say 'distinct action' (`distinct_action`); round-1 C07 says 'new distinct activity'. Reading 1: distinct_action (matches v2.6 Stage 6 code). Reading 2: distinct.

Direction of 'component of program': the relation is asymmetric (A is a component of program B). v2.6 relations are unordered pairs (left_input, right_input) with no direction. Reading 1: one code plus a fixed order rule (left is the component, right is the program). Reading 2: two inverse codes (component_of_program and has_component). C07's wording ('component of span k') reads as the first: the span being coded is the component.

Direction of 'governs': also asymmetric (a policy governs the tools it approves, R-017). Same two readings: one code with a fixed order (left governs right), or two inverse codes (governs and governed_by).

Meaning change for 'component of program': in v2.6 a component relation merged both observations into one activity identity (same as same_activity and shared_participation). R-017 now says each named component is its own activity, linked to the program. The code can stay the same, but whether it merges or only links is not settled by the value list.
One pair, two relations: a program-level policy can be both a component of the program and govern a sibling tool; a single-answer relation cannot hold both. No precedence is ruled.

'Unresolved' versus 'unknown': the item's draft downgrade target is unknown (R-045), while the list has its own 'unresolved'. Reading 1: a downgraded relation becomes unresolved (no new token). Reading 2: it becomes unknown, giving two codes for 'could not tell'.

No overlap was found among same activity, shared participation, governs and distinct once direction is fixed; shared participation is the joint-activity case of same identity (v2.6 requires two documented participants).

Unit of the within-page answer: C07 asks per span ('new distinct activity / same as span k / ...'), which is one answer per span against an earlier span; R-017 and r2#22 give a pairwise list. Reading 1: per span, relative to one earlier span k (the first span is always 'new'). Reading 2: per pair of spans, as at Stage 6. Under reading 1, 'new distinct activity' is a span label rather than a pair relation, and the shared list then has no value for the first span.
'Not an activity' is a property of one span, not of a pair; it sits in the same list only within a page.

flags: Spelling of the two new values: the SPEC text gives them as phrases, not codes. Candidates: downgraded_quote_not_stating_value or downgraded_not_entailed; set_by_rule, deterministic or deterministic_rule.
'Set by rule' needs a companion rule id. Reading 1: a separate rule_id field beside support_status. Reading 2: the rule id inside the value (e.g. set_by_rule:<id>), which makes the list open-ended.

R-041 also says a page verdict's 'support status says `downgraded`'. Reading 1: this means one of the downgraded_* values (r2#40 names 'downgraded: low confidence' and 'downgraded: no quote'). Reading 2: a seventh, bare `downgraded` value for verdicts. Reading 1 is supported by r2#40's wording.
'Set by rule' versus 'not_required' can overlap: a value fixed by a gate (e.g. not asked) or a negative value set by a rule needs no quote under both. No precedence is given.
Two downgrade reasons can hold at once (no quote and low probability). The list has one value per code; no precedence is given.
Coverage: a code that was never asked (not asked) still needs a support status; Reading 1: not_required; Reading 2: set_by_rule (the gate is a rule).

flags: Spelling of 'not asked': the codebook draft uses not_asked; the agent draft behind r2#16 used `_NA_` for the same token (planning/t010/codebook-review/review-r2-consistency.json R2C04 option a). R-045 leaves the spelling to the PI.

`_NA_` survives elsewhere: R-041 still lists `_NA_` beside not_documented and unknown as needing no support, and v2.5 uses `_NA_` for fields on a row with no activity. Reading 1: `_NA_` is the old spelling of not asked and goes. Reading 2: `_NA_` stays as a fourth, structural token for 'no activity on this row'.

'Unknown' covers two cases (stated but undeterminable; downgraded). Not an overlap with the other tokens, but a downgraded code and a genuinely undeterminable one cannot be told apart from the token alone; the support status carries the difference.

'Unresolved' (activity relations, observed actor) and the mechanical page verdict 'not assessable' act like missing values but are not in this set. Reading 1: they are ordinary values of their items. Reading 2: they map onto unknown / not asked.
Frozen institutional-questionnaire items keep signed spellings (e.g. none_reported, none_documented, none) with a mapping row; the mapping rows are not drafted here.
